title: Cloudflare Turns CI Pipelines into TypeScript Workflows
gist: Cloudflare released @cloudflare/ci, an SDK that defines CI pipelines in TypeScript rather than YAML, running each step as a durable Cloudflare Workflow with checkpointed retries. It deeply binds Cloudflare's platform (Workflows, Sandboxes, Containers, Durable Objects, R2) and ships a separate self-healing example that patches failures via a Workers AI agent using Moonshot's Kimi model.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's @cloudflare/ci SDK lets developers define CI pipelines in TypeScript instead of YAML, running each step as a durable Cloudflare Workflow so a failed step retries with state preserved and a run can restart from that step rather than repeating the whole pipeline.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Step-level checkpointed retries eliminate full-pipeline reruns, a concrete resilience gain for CI.
insights.quote: In essence, a CI/CD pipeline is just a Workflow,
insights.locator: Each stage maps to a Workflow step paragraph

insights.claim: Dependency caching stores an install step's result as a Sandbox filesystem snapshot in an R2 bucket for reuse, and a new events field in Wrangler config triggers a Workflow directly on a cf.artifacts.repo.pushed event, replacing earlier subscription, queue and consumer wiring.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Snapshot caching and event triggers remove common CI glue code for teams already on Cloudflare's stack.
insights.locator: Two mechanisms address familiar CI pain points paragraph

insights.claim: A working @cloudflare/ci pipeline binds Workflows, Sandboxes, Containers and Durable Objects plus R2 for caching and targets the Workers runtime rather than Node.js, making it a platform commitment rather than a drop-in CI replacement.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Deep platform coupling is the price of the resumable-state benefit, key for teams weighing vendor lock-in.
insights.locator: A working pipeline also binds paragraph

insights.claim: Cloudflare makes the opposite trade to Dagger, which runs pipelines in containers on any OCI-compatible system caching by content address, by binding execution to Workflows and Sandboxes in return for resumable state.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Portability versus resumable state is the core architectural choice distinguishing code-based CI tools.
insights.locator: Cloudflare is not the first paragraph

insights.claim: Because runner commands execute inside retryable Workflow steps, any command with external side effects must be idempotent or a retry will duplicate it, and the SDK returns raw command output in CiRunnerResult.logs without secret redaction.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Idempotency requirements and unredacted logs are real production gotchas teams must design around.
insights.locator: two constraints that matter in production paragraph

insights.claim: Cloudflare published self-healing as a separate example that wraps the pipeline in try/catch and calls an application-owned agent running a Think harness over Workers AI, using Moonshot's Kimi coding model to propose a patch and commit it to a branch while leaving the original run failed until an engineer merges it.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A repair agent that stops short of merging is a transferable pattern for safe AI-assisted CI remediation.
